newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates gain on short supply.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates gain on short supply.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates gained on Wednesday as demand outpaced supply and are likely to remain firm in the coming days as arrival of the 1997/98 (July-June) crop has not fully picked up, dealers said.

"Cotton rates in Sindh province rose on mills' demand from Punjab province where arrival of new crop has not picked up," dealer Kishan Chand said. "The rates are likely to remain firm in the next couple of weeks as supply is shorter than demand."
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was quoted around 2,250 ($55.47) rupees per maund (37.32 kg).
